item.text: The underlying TTL cache already checks expiration on `Get`, but its `Keys` method includes expired entries until `DeleteExpired` runs. I’m adding a scheduled eviction check at operation entry, with active-item filtering for `Keys` and `Values` so both stay accurate between sweeps.

The cache tests pass. I found one capacity detail worth fixing before finishing: the TTL library’s `Items()` method changes recency while listing entries, which could change which item a size limit evicts. I’m switching collection reads to its read-only traversal and will rerun the tests.

item.text:
Implemented opportunistic expiration cleanup using an atomic eviction deadline. `Add`, `AddWithTTL`, `Get`, `GetWithLoader`, `Keys`, and the new `Values` method now trigger eviction; collection reads expose only active entries. Loader results retain their TTL, and collection reads preserve the size limit’s eviction order.

Added tests for 10 ms expiration, loader reloads, and size limit behavior. `go test ./utils/cache`, `go test ./core/scrobbler`, and `git diff --check` passed.
